questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The Helmholtz free energy $F$ of a system in thermal equilibrium at temperature $T$ is related to its canonical partition function $Z$ by:
questions.explanationEn: In the canonical ensemble, the bridge relation connecting statistical mechanics to thermodynamics is $F = -k_B T \ln Z$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A Carnot refrigerator extracts heat from a cold reservoir at $T_C$ and rejects it to a hot reservoir at $T_H$. If the Carnot efficiency of the corresponding heat engine operating between the same two reservoirs is $\eta$, the coefficient of performance (COP) of the refrigerator is:
questions.explanationEn: With $\eta = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H}$, we have $\frac{T_C}{T_H} = 1 - \eta$. The refrigerator COP is $\text{COP}_R = \frac{T_C}{T_H - T_C} = \frac{T_C/T_H}{1 - T_C/T_H} = \frac{1 - \eta}{\eta}$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: According to Ehrenfest's classification, across a second-order phase transition at constant pressure, which of the following quantities exhibits a finite jump discontinuity?
questions.explanationEn: In a second-order phase transition, $G$ and its first derivatives ($S = -(\partial G/\partial T)_P$ and $V = (\partial G/\partial P)_T$) are continuous, while its second derivatives—such as $C_P = -T(\partial^2 G/\partial T^2)_P$, $\beta$, and $\kappa_T$—show finite jump discontinuities. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For an equilibrium photon gas (blackbody radiation) in a cavity of volume $V$ at temperature $T$, the equation of state relating radiation pressure $P$ to internal energy density $u = U/V$ is:
questions.explanationEn: Because photons are massless ultra-relativistic particles ($E = pc$), the radiation pressure of an isotropic photon gas is $P = \frac{1}{3} u$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For a classical ideal gas at temperature $T$, the probability distribution $P(v_x)$ of the $x$-component of molecular velocity $v_x \in (-\infty, \infty)$ has its maximum at:
questions.explanationEn: The 1D velocity component distribution is a centered Gaussian, $P(v_x) = \sqrt{\frac{m}{2\pi k_B T}} \exp\left(-\frac{m v_x^2}{2k_B T}\right)$, which attains its single maximum at $v_x = 0$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: If $\kappa_T = -\frac{1}{V}\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial P}\right)_T$ is the isothermal compressibility and $\kappa_S = -\frac{1}{V}\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial P}\right)_S$ is the adiabatic compressibility of a thermodynamic system, then the difference $\kappa_T - \kappa_S$ equals:
questions.explanationEn: Using $\frac{\kappa_T}{\kappa_S} = \frac{C_P}{C_V}$, we have $\kappa_T - \kappa_S = \kappa_T\left(1 - \frac{C_V}{C_P}\right) = \frac{\kappa_T}{C_P}(C_P - C_V)$. Substituting $C_P - C_V = \frac{TV\beta^2}{\kappa_T}$ yields $\kappa_T - \kappa_S = \frac{TV\beta^2}{C_P}$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: One mole of an ideal monatomic gas is taken from an initial state $(V_0, T_0)$ to a final state $(2V_0, 4T_0)$. The change in entropy $\Delta S$ of the gas is:
questions.explanationEn: For $1\text{ mole}$ of an ideal monatomic gas ($C_V = \frac{3}{2}R$), the entropy change is $\Delta S = C_V\ln\left(\frac{T_f}{T_i}\right) + R\ln\left(\frac{V_f}{V_i}\right) = \frac{3}{2}R\ln 4 + R\ln 2 = 3R\ln 2 + R\ln 2 = 4R\ln 2$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: An ideal Stirling engine using an ideal gas operates between a hot reservoir at $T_H$ and a cold reservoir at $T_C$ with an ideal (100% efficient) regenerator. Its thermal efficiency is:
questions.explanationEn: In an ideal Stirling cycle with a perfect regenerator, the heat rejected during the isochoric cooling leg is stored and completely returned during the isochoric heating leg. All external heat exchange occurs reversibly along the two isotherms at $T_H$ and $T_C$, so $\eta = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H}$, identical to the Carnot efficiency. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In terms of volume $V$, temperature $T$, pressure $P$, volume expansivity $\beta = \frac{1}{V}\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial T}\right)_P$, and isothermal compressibility $\kappa_T = -\frac{1}{V}\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial P}\right)_T$, the partial derivative $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial P}\right)_T$ is equal to:
questions.explanationEn: From $dU = T\,dS - P\,dV$, dividing by $dP$ at constant $T$ gives $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial P}\right)_T = T\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial P}\right)_T - P\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial P}\right)_T$. Using Maxwell's relation $\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial P}\right)_T = -\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial T}\right)_P = -V\beta$ and $\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial P}\right)_T = -V\kappa_T$, we obtain $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial P}\right)_T = -TV\beta + PV\kappa_T = V(P\kappa_T - T\beta)$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider a classical two-dimensional ideal gas of particles of mass $m$ adsorbed on a flat surface at temperature $T$. The most probable speed $v_{\text{mp}}$ of the particles in 2D is:
questions.explanationEn: In 2D, the speed distribution is $f_{2D}(v) = \frac{m}{k_B T} v \exp\left(-\frac{mv^2}{2k_B T}\right)$. Setting $\frac{df_{2D}}{dv} = 0$ gives $\left(1 - \frac{mv^2}{k_B T}\right) e^{-mv^2/(2k_B T)} = 0 \implies v_{\text{mp}} = \sqrt{\frac{k_B T}{m}}$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the canonical ensemble at inverse temperature $\beta = (k_B T)^{-1}$ with partition function $Z = \sum_i e^{-\beta E_i}$, which of the following identities is/are CORRECT?
questions.explanationEn: Direct differentiation of $\ln Z$: (A) $-\frac{\partial \ln Z}{\partial \beta} = \frac{1}{Z}\sum_i E_i e^{-\beta E_i} = \langle E \rangle$ (True); (B) $\frac{\partial^2 \ln Z}{\partial \beta^2} = -\frac{\partial \langle E \rangle}{\partial \beta} = \langle E^2 \rangle - \langle E \rangle^2$ (True); (C) $C_V = \frac{\partial \langle E \rangle}{\partial T} = -k_B\beta^2 \frac{\partial \langle E \rangle}{\partial \beta} = k_B \beta^2 \frac{\partial^2 \ln Z}{\partial \beta^2}$ (True); (D) $S = \frac{\langle E \rangle - F}{T} = k_B\beta \langle E \rangle + k_B\ln Z = k_B\ln Z - k_B\beta \frac{\partial \ln Z}{\partial \beta}$ (True). Hence, (A), (B), (C), and (D) are all correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: One mole of an ideal diatomic gas ($\gamma = \frac{7}{5}$) undergoes a reversible process $A \to B$ in which its pressure and volume double: $(P_0, V_0) \to (2P_0, 2V_0)$ along a straight line in the $P$-$V$ diagram. Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: The work done by the gas is $\frac{3}{2}P_0 V_0$
The change in internal energy is $\frac{15}{2}P_0 V_0$
The heat absorbed by the gas is $9 P_0 V_0$
questions.explanationEn: From $PV = RT$: $T_B = \frac{(2P_0)(2V_0)}{R} = 4T_0$ (A True). Work done is the trapezoidal area: $W = \frac{1}{2}(P_0 + 2P_0)(2V_0 - V_0) = \frac{3}{2}P_0 V_0$ (B True). Internal energy change: $\Delta U = \frac{5}{2}R(4T_0 - T_0) = \frac{15}{2}P_0 V_0$ (C True). By the first law: $Q = \Delta U + W = \frac{15}{2}P_0 V_0 + \frac{3}{2}P_0 V_0 = 9P_0 V_0$ (D True). Hence, (A), (B), (C), and (D) are all correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For one mole of a real gas described by the van der Waals equation $\left(P + \frac{a}{V^2}\right)(V - b) = RT$, which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: At the critical point, $\left(\frac{\partial P}{\partial V}\right)_T = 0$ and $\left(\frac{\partial^2 P}{\partial V^2}\right)_T = 0$
The internal energy $U$ depends on both temperature $T$ and volume $V$
The molar heat capacity $C_V$ depends explicitly on volume $V$ at fixed $T$
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: The critical point is a horizontal inflection point on the critical isotherm. (B) True: Solving the two derivative conditions gives $V_c = 3b$, $P_c = \frac{a}{27b^2}$, $T_c = \frac{8a}{27Rb}$. (C) True: $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial V}\right)_T = \frac{a}{V^2} \neq 0$, so $U(T, V) = U_{\text{ideal}}(T) - \frac{a}{V}$. (D) False: $\left(\frac{\partial C_V}{\partial V}\right)_T = T\left(\frac{\partial^2 P}{\partial T^2}\right)_V = 0$, so $C_V$ is independent of $V$. Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A thermodynamic system has equation of state $P = f(T)/V$ (where $f(T)$ is a positive function of $T$ alone). Which of the following statement(s) MUST be true?
optionsEn: In general, $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial V}\right)_T = \frac{T f'(T) - f(T)}{V}$
If $f(T) = c T^2$ ($c > 0$), then $\left(\frac{\partial C_V}{\partial V}\right)_T = \frac{2cT}{V}$
For any $f(T)$, the internal energy $U$ is strictly independent of volume $V$
questions.explanationEn: Using $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial V}\right)_T = T\left(\frac{\partial P}{\partial T}\right)_V - P = \frac{T f'(T) - f(T)}{V}$ (B True). When $f(T) = RT$, $Tf'(T) - f(T) = 0$ (A True). Using $\left(\frac{\partial C_V}{\partial V}\right)_T = T\left(\frac{\partial^2 P}{\partial T^2}\right)_V = \frac{T f''(T)}{V}$, for $f(T) = cT^2$ we get $\frac{2cT}{V}$ (C True). Since $Tf'(T) - f(T) \neq 0$ for nonlinear $f(T)$, $U$ depends on $V$ in general (D False). Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A system consists of $6$ distinguishable non-interacting spin-$1/2$ particles. The number of microstates having exactly $4$ spins aligned upward and $2$ spins aligned downward is ______ (Answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: The number of ways to choose $4$ upward spins out of $6$ distinguishable particles is $\Omega = \binom{6}{4} = \frac{6!}{4!\,2!} = 15$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For a gas of non-interacting bosons in thermal equilibrium at temperature $T$, the mean occupation number of a single-particle state with energy $\epsilon = \mu + k_B T \ln 3$ is ______ (Round off to 1 decimal place).
questions.explanationEn: By the Bose-Einstein distribution, $\langle n(\epsilon) \rangle = \frac{1}{e^{(\epsilon - \mu)/(k_B T)} - 1} = \frac{1}{e^{\ln 3} - 1} = \frac{1}{3 - 1} = 0.5$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The translational kinetic energy per unit volume of a monatomic ideal gas in a vessel is $300\text{ kJ/m}^3$. The pressure of the gas is ______ $\text{kPa}$ (Answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: For an ideal gas in 3D, $P = \frac{2}{3}u_{\text{tr}} = \frac{2}{3}(300\text{ kPa}) = 200\text{ kPa}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: One mole of an ideal monatomic gas initially at $800\text{ K}$ expands reversibly and adiabatically to $8$ times its initial volume. The final temperature of the gas, in $\text{K}$, is ______ (Answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: For an ideal monatomic gas, $\gamma = \frac{5}{3}$, so $\gamma - 1 = \frac{2}{3}$. Along a reversible adiabat, $T_2 = T_1\left(\frac{V_1}{V_2}\right)^{\gamma - 1} = 800 \times \left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{2/3} = \frac{800}{4} = 200\text{ K}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: During a thermodynamic process, a gas absorbs $500\text{ J}$ of heat while doing $180\text{ J}$ of mechanical work on its surroundings. The change in internal energy of the gas is ______ $\text{J}$ (Answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: By the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = Q - W = 500\text{ J} - 180\text{ J} = 320\text{ J}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Kinetic Theory and Thermodynamics (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: An ideal monatomic gas ($\gamma = \frac{5}{3}$) initially at $300\text{ K}$ and $1\text{ atm}$ is compressed reversibly and adiabatically until its pressure reaches $32\text{ atm}$. The final temperature of the gas is ______ $\text{K}$ (Answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Along a reversible adiabat, $T_2 = T_1\left(\frac{P_2}{P_1}\right)^{(\gamma - 1)/\gamma} = 300 \times (32)^{2/5} = 300 \times (2^5)^{2/5} = 300 \times 4 = 1200\text{ K}$.
